grade_reason: The only evidence at level A is a letter she co-signed that calls advanced AI a technology that poses an existential threat. No statement in her own individual words about catastrophic AI risk was found.
notes: Seven web searches ran, none refused. The grade rests entirely on the co-signed letter. Quotes from the Van Hollen page and the Sun-Times article were read through a page-fetching tool that summarises pages; the existential-threat sentence was confirmed in a dedicated check, but the Sun-Times and slowdown quotes were returned once each as the tool's exact quotes and should be checked by eye. The tool would not print the full slowdown sentence in one piece, so only the confirmed fragment is quoted; the tool also reported the letter says AI capabilities may "accelerate beyond our ability to understand or control them" (fragment, not used as a statement). The letter PDF on commerce.senate.gov could not be read (no PDF reader available). Sun-Times date taken from the article URL. Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act: no source found showing Duckworth as a co-sponsor; the official cosponsor list on Congress.gov was not checked. A search result said she co-sponsored a bill to repeal the federal moratorium on state AI laws (Benton summary, not opened, not about catastrophic risk) and joined a May 2026 statement after the Trump-Xi summit (content not seen). Her other AI material (AI toys, data centers, military tech talent, algorithmic bias) is outside the project's scope.
